findings.explanation: The SPL searches only nir:latency_flow, fabric_latency, latency and nxos:nir:latency. It never reads cisco:aci:interface or cisco:aci:syslog, so the eqpt drop counters, counter-wrap and syslog clock-skew signals that the title and description promise cannot be produced.
findings.suggested_fix: Either remove the interface and syslog lanes from the text, or state that they require a separate search (for example, UC-18.1.6 for drop counters).

findings.explanation: NIR was 'Network Insights Resources', since folded into Nexus Dashboard Insights. I could not find a documented export that streams per-flow ingress/egress nanosecond timestamps to Splunk over gRPC, or these field names. NDI exports anomalies and flow records through Kafka, syslog or email. The sourcetype and fields look custom or invented.
findings.suggested_fix: Name the actual NDI export mechanism (Kafka / syslog export of flow analytics) and the fields it carries, or label the sourcetype as a customer-built collector with an example payload.

findings.explanation: Splunkbase 1897 is 'Cisco ACI Add-on for Splunk Enterprise' (TA_cisco-ACI) and is marked deprecated. detailedImplementation also calls it 'Splunk_TA_cisco-aci'. Cisco DC Networking (7777) is the current app.
findings.suggested_fix: Use the correct add-on name, mark it deprecated, and lead with Cisco DC Networking (7777).

findings.explanation: None of these labels exist in the SPL, the data sources or knownFalsePositives. The runbook pages on states nobody can observe.
findings.quote: **`epg_relocation_path_swap`** rehearsals versus stealth **`microburst_lag_uplink_skew`** bursts ... **`ptp_skew_adjustment_event`** stamps ... **`grpc_interval_change_window`** shifts summarized under **`knownFalsePositives`**
findings.suggested_fix: Remove the invented labels, or define them in the SPL and the false-positive list.

findings.explanation: A generic boilerplate block repeats the app and dataSources text verbatim and adds generic tuning advice. The 'Governance cadence' and 'Closing hygiene' paragraphs are also filler with no ACI-specific guidance.
findings.quote:
Step 1 — Configure data collection

Install and configure the upstream Splunk app or TA ... index=* sourcetype="cisco:aci:nir:latency_flow" earliest=-15m | head 5
findings.suggested_fix: Delete the duplicated Step 1/Step 2 block and the governance filler, and keep the ingestion, search-design and validation steps.

findings.explanation: An NSX crosswalk CSV has nothing to do with ACI in-fabric latency and is not used by the SPL. It also causes the vmware equipment tag.
findings.quote: **`sourcetype=vmware_nsx:aci_crosswalk`** (optional CSV sink) tags east-west workload batches
findings.suggested_fix: Remove the NSX crosswalk lane and the vmware equipment tag.

findings.explanation: APIC eqpt*Total cumulative counters (bytesCum/pktsCum) are 64-bit. The SPL fields eqptIngr_prev32 / eqptIngr_curr32 do not correspond to any APIC attribute. The 'Separate RBAC identities: network-admin' line also names a role APIC does not have (built-ins include read-all, ops, fabric-admin).
findings.quote: compute **`wrap_seen`** when sequential epochs imply **32-bit** rollover
findings.suggested_fix: Confirm the counter width in the APIC MIM. If it is 64-bit, drop the 32-bit wrap logic, and use an existing APIC role name.

findings.suggested_fix: Link a specific Cisco document (for example the NDI flow-analytics / latency user guide), or remove the entry.

findings.explanation: The data feed and field names are unverified and partly invented, and the reviewer is an automated agent pass.
findings.suggested_fix: Downgrade the status until an ACI/NDI SME confirms the telemetry export and fields.

firewalled_field_flags.issue: case() returns null for every row without latency_us, so the burst_proxy, wrap_hint, nir_gap and skew branches only fire on rows that already have latency, and the first matching branch (latency_us>=500) hides the rest. The eqpt and syslog inputs are not in the base search anyway, so most of the fault taxonomy can never appear.

'grpc_iv_sec<=1 AND maint_txt=""' labels high-frequency telemetry as a fault ('grpc_hi_freq_window'), which is a configuration choice and not a fabric problem. The skew_warn regex on _raw ('clock|ntp|ptp|skew') will match unrelated text.
The title promises 'Microburst/HBM Drops' and 'Clock Skew', which the SPL cannot detect because it does not search the eqpt or syslog sourcetypes.

summary: The goal (in-fabric latency, microburst drops and clock skew) is coherent, but the UC rests on custom sourcetypes and per-flow timestamp fields it cannot show exist, lists data sources the SPL never searches, and pads detailedImplementation with invented fault labels and a duplicated generic step section.
